t:
(a) Briefing Required.—Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics, in consultation with the Secretary of the Army, shall provide a briefing to the congressional defense committees on the acquisition strategy for the Ground Mobility Vehicle for use with the Global Response Force of the 82nd Airborne Division. 
    (b) Elements.—The briefing under subsection (a) shall include an assessment of the following:
        (1) The feasability of acquiring the Ground Mobility Vehicle—
            (A) as a commercially available off-the-shelf item (as such term is defined in section 104 of title 41, United States Code); or 
            (B) as a modified version of such an item.  
        (2) Whether acquiring the Ground Mobility Vehicle in a manner described in paragraph (1) would satisfy the requirements of the program and reduce the life-cycle cost of the program. 
        (3) Whether the acquisition strategy for the Ground Mobility Vehicle meets the focus areas specified in the most recent version of the Better Buying Power initiative of the Secretary of Defense. 
        (4) Whether including an active safety system in the Ground Mobility Vehicle, such as the electronic stability control system used on the joint light tactical vehicle, would reduce the risk of vehicle rollover.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "in consultation with" and a required briefing amount to participation. But the consultation is between two federal officials, and the briefing goes to congressional committees, all of which are inside the federal government. No state, tribe, company, expert, or member of the public is brought into any federal decision; the mention of commercially available off-the-shelf items is only a topic for assessment, not a process involving outside parties.
fable.s: the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics, in consultation with the Secretary of the Army, shall provide a briefing to the congressional defense committees

qwen_block.w: The section requires a briefing to be provided to congressional defense committees. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to it is an intra-governmental action, not participation by outside parties. The consultation mentioned is between two federal officials (Under Secretary of Defense and Secretary of the Army), which is also internal coordination.
qwen_block.s: the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics, in consultation with the Secretary of the Army, shall provide a briefing to the congressional defense committees

opus.w: The only consultation is between two Defense Department officials, and the briefing goes to congressional committees. Both kinds of interaction stay inside the federal government. No state, expert, company or member of the public is consulted, and nobody outside the government gets a right to sue. Procedural words like "consultation" and "briefing" are not enough unless someone outside the federal government is involved.
opus.s: the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics, in consultation with the Secretary of the Army, shall provide a briefing to the congressional defense committees
opus.b: The tempting reading is that the phrase "in consultation with the Secretary of the Army" and the required briefing to the congressional defense committees count as participation. That reading fails because the Under Secretary, the Secretary of the Army and the congressional committees are all inside the federal government, and nothing in the section brings in anyone outside it.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires a briefing to congressional defense committees, which are part of the federal government. The consultation mentioned is between two federal officials (Under Secretary of Defense and Secretary of Army), which is intra-governmental coordination. Since all actors involved (federal agencies and Congress) are inside the federal government, this does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics, in consultation with the Secretary of the Army, shall provide a briefing to the congressional defense committees
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: The phrase "in consultation with the Secretary of the Army" suggests participation because it involves coordination between officials. However, both the Under Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of the Army are federal officials inside the government. Intra-governmental consultation does not constitute participation under the definition. Furthermore, the briefing is directed to congressional defense committees, and Congress is also inside the federal government. Therefore, no outside party is involved in the decision-making process described.
